summary.headline: Laser Power Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 2.1% YoY to ₹628 crore, with ₹2,543 crore order book and first HCLS and 220 kV underground orders.
summary.overview: Management framed the quarter as Laser Power's entry into high-voltage transmission, citing a ₹72.76 crore Power Grid HCLS conductor order and a ₹44 crore CESC 220 kV underground cabling order. Standalone revenue was ₹628 crore (up 2.1% YoY, up 20.5% QoQ) with EBITDA of ₹76 crore at a 12.1% margin versus 13% a year earlier. Working capital rose to ₹1,159 crore, with working capital days down to 166 from 183 in Q1, and management targets a 25–40 day cut by Q4 FY27 and positive operating cash flow. The call was light on quantified guidance, and several transcript passages were garbled, so some figures should be verified against the filing.

financial_highlights.change: Down sharply YoY (vs ₹212 crore), as stated on the call

financial_highlights.value: ₹31 crore (as stated, possibly H1 PAT; garbled in transcript)
₹357 crore in Q2; ~₹449 crore in H1 FY27

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹524 crore, up 29.9% YoY. Management guides manufacturing margin at about 10–11% and says segment margins are not reported separately because plants and costs are shared.

segments.name: ETC (EPC)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹104 crore as stated on the call, with management attributing the shortfall to heavy rains; about ₹100 crore of EPC revenue was deferred. Management guides EPC margins at roughly 14–16%.

guidance_outlook: Working capital days to improve by 25–40 days by Q4 FY27, driven by procurement discipline, faster certification, timely billing and collections.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive by Q4 FY27 (transcript says 'April 23', likely a transcription error).
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided to a stable 12.5–13% range.
Seasonality: H1 is typically about 42% of annual revenue and H2 the balance. An analyst's derived FY27 revenue of about ₹2,700 crore and EBITDA of about ₹340 crore was not confirmed by management.
Mix target: EPC to manufacturing at about 75:25. Manufacturing mix about 80–90% cable and 10–15% conductor, with a shift toward specialised conductors.
Capacity utilisation expected at about 70% for FY27 as capacity expansion is added.
capex_capacity: Proposed integrated power cable and conductor manufacturing facility at Hidya Sardar Industrial Park, Kharagpur (West Bengal); WBIDC gave a provisional LoI and in-principle approval for about 40 acres.
Investment timing and scale to be aligned with demand visibility, product strategy and expected returns; phased approach.
Management says the new capacity will be on existing land at Kharagpur, with no capacity or capex figure given.
Current capacity utilisation about 70–75%, per management.
demand_pricing: Power Grid HCLS/reconductoring order of ₹72.76 crore, the company's first commercial HCLS order, under a licensing deal with TS Conductors (USA). Work covers a transmission line in Assam, and the product was qualified over about 18 months.
CESC order of ₹44 crore for 33 kV and 220 kV underground cabling, with about one-year execution; management expects 14–16% margins on such ETC projects.
Management says the mix of government and private revenue in manufacturing is about 50:50.
Pricing: management says the newer-generation conductor has cost advantages and that price competition from new licensees will be countered by these advantages.
Order pipeline: management says manufacturing orders take about six months to deliver and ETC cycles run 1.5–2 years, and expects more order announcements by year end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin upside from specialised conductors and HV cables, and can margins move to 13–14%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mix shift toward specialised conductors and underground cabling, which are higher-margin products, will lift margins over time. No quantified target was given beyond the 12.5–13% guide.

qa_highlights.question: What are the CESC project value, timeline and profitability, and does it open larger EHV underground opportunities?
qa_highlights.answer: Value is about ₹44 crore with roughly one-year execution. Management expects 14–16% margins and said the project builds 220 kV credentials for larger opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EPC revenue fall, and by how much was it deferred?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall to heavy rains in project areas and said about ₹100 crore of EPC revenue was deferred into later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why are working capital days stretched, and what is the normalised level?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is elevated because of rain-related execution delays. Management targets a 25–40 day reduction by Q4 FY27 and says operating cash flow should turn positive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity and capex for the Kharagpur site?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no capacity or capex figures and said the project is being phased, with timing aligned to demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book split between conductors and cables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 85% cable and 15% conductor, roughly in line with the existing mix.

risks_watch: Working capital: inventory rose to ₹946 crore and days remain high at 166, so the Q4 FY27 target of a 25–40 day cut and positive operating cash flow need to be tracked.
Execution: rain-related delays deferred about ₹100 crore of EPC revenue; the Power Grid and CESC projects are the first test of new HCLS and 220 kV underground execution.
Pricing competition as more licensees of the TS Conductors technology enter tenders.
Order inflow of ₹357 crore in Q2 was below Q2 revenue of ₹628 crore, so the order book is shrinking relative to billing; management did not name larger H2 orders.
Capex for Kharagpur is undefined, and segment margins are not disclosed, so there is limited visibility into the mix effect.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategic story of entering HV transmission and on the Power Grid and CESC wins. Noticeably cautious on the numbers: it was vague on capex, product-level margins and the H2 pipeline, and it attributed weakness to rain.
key_quotes: Together these developments move us up the value chain from a company known largely for distribution grade products and ETC to one with credentials in high voltage transmission.
This is laser's first commercial HCLS order.
Our approach will remain safe and disciplined.
So we see that to be normalized by Q4 and that's how we expect our cash flow operating cash flow also to be positive by the year.

adds.what: Proposed integrated power cable and conductor manufacturing facility at Hidya Sardar Industrial Park, Kharagpur (West Bengal); provisional LoI for ~40 acres, ph

growth.why: No quantified revenue guidance; management held EBITDA margin at 12.5–13% and targets 25–40 day working capital cut by Q4 FY27, while the ~₹2,543 crore order book (₹357 crore Q2 inflow) and a phased Kharagpur plant with no capex or timing give only partial backing for growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management held consolidated EBITDA margin at 12.5-13% (Q2 at 12.1% standalone vs 13% a year ago), and says specialised conductors and HV cables (14-16% EPC margin, 10-11% manufacturing) will lift margins over time, but gave no quantified target beyond the guide.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Kharagpur integrated cable and conductor plant has only a provisional WBIDC LoI for about 40 acres with no capacity or capex figure, and timing is tied to demand visibility; current utilisation is about 70-75%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Manufacturing revenue grew 29.9% YoY to Rs 524 crore, and the Power Grid HCLS (Rs 72.76 crore) and CESC (Rs 44 crore) orders add HV credentials, but Q2 order inflow of Rs 357 crore was below Q2 revenue of Rs 628 crore and about Rs 100 crore of EPC revenue was deferred by rain.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only about 70-75% with no capex figure disclosed for Kharagpur, so a sized capex announcement is conditional on demand visibility and returns rather than near-term.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No quantified revenue guidance was given, H1 revenue was Rs 1,150 crore, and Q2 EBITDA margin of 12.1% was below the year-ago 13%, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Rs 100 crore of EPC revenue was deferred by rains, inventory rose to Rs 946 crore from Rs 710 crore, and the H2 pipeline was not quantified, so execution slippage is a real risk to the 12.5-13% margin and working capital targets.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Entry into HV transmission via the first HCLS conductor order (Rs 72.76 crore, licensed from TS Conductors, qualified over about 18 months) and the 220 kV underground cable order (Rs 44 crore, about one-year execution) represent new product lines, with management expecting more order announcements by year end.

rows.label: Working capital days cut 25-40 days by Q4 FY27
rows.why: Days fell to 166 from 183 in Q1, and management targets a 25-40 day reduction plus positive operating cash flow by Q4 FY27, though inventory rose to Rs 946 crore from Rs 710 crore and the transcript date for cash flow is garbled.

rows.label: Order book ~Rs 2,543 crore, more order announcements by year end
rows.why: Order book of about Rs 2,543 crore (about 2 years of Q2 run-rate revenue) with Q2 inflow of Rs 357 crore below billing of Rs 628 crore, and management expects more announcements but named no larger H2 orders.

rows.label: Price competition from new TS Conductors licensees
rows.why: Management says newer-generation conductor cost advantages will counter new licensees entering tenders, but no pricing figures were disclosed and the risk is flagged in the brief.

tone.note: Management was confident on the HV transmission entry and the Power Grid and CESC wins, but cautious and vague on capex, product margins and H2 pipeline, attributing weakness to rain; analysts pressed on margin upside, EPC deferral and working capital.
